0c04dd0f-498b-4bc9-9451-070da386823e.summary_md: Jesse cruised to a 20-7 record (+1651 spread) at King's Cup 2019, headlined by a monstrous 709-274 demolition of Cedric Lewis in Round 12 and a 199-point rout of Henry Yeo. Nigel Richards proved the toughest matchup, splitting their four encounters 2-2, with two narrow one-point squeakers (409-408 over Thacha Koowirat, 410-409 over Jakkrit Klaphajone) showing the margins could be razor-thin even in a winning tournament. Jesse's play was sharp overall — a 1.75 average mistakes score and a strong 93.2% bingo find rate (69/74) — though five missed bingos (including MEAGRES, AM(B)ITION, and AGEnTIV(A)(L)) and a trio of late-tournament losses to Akshay Bhandarkar, Yong Jian Rong, and Richards himself cost some ground. Akshay Bhandarkar was the other standout opponent, taking two of three meetings and playing with notable precision down the stretch.
0c04dd0f-498b-4bc9-9451-070da386823e.title: King's Cup 2019

12dd6445-9dfc-4859-b110-6fcd966234b7.summary_md: Jesse ran the table at 13-1 (+1778) in Collins League Season 20, topping Division 12 of 15 with standout blowouts like the 587-275 demolition of Pam Field and 515-260 over Bhawani Cheerath, with the only loss coming to dang3rous (374-537) despite a clean game. His 33/33 bingo find rate versus opponents' 19/36 tells the story of the gap, and his 1.32 mistakes score ranks 1st of 208 qualified players league-wide. Most win probability actually bled away early (25 errors, 41.0% lost) and in the midgame (26 errors, 28.1% lost), driven by ordinary tactical slips rather than missed bingos — the costliest was Round 9 against Bhawani Cheerath, choosing 10F HARdIER (78) over the superior K4 HERb(A)RIA (90), a 5.5% win-probability swing. Since Collins League play voids phonies outright, the zero-phony record here is simply the rule in action, not a credit to either side, and the mistakes-score figures aren't comparable to challenge-rule tournament results.
12dd6445-9dfc-4859-b110-6fcd966234b7.title: Collins League - Season 20

19a0eadf-f17a-409e-bf32-46543a2fd6fd.summary_md: Jesse finished 9-3 (+1042) in Collins League Season 18, taking 2nd of 13 in Division 14, with dominant wins over JOHN DIXON (+256), NickTheMe1on (+288), and Vegewey (+169) offset by losses to Ishika S, Laurie Cohen, and Lu Bunker. Most of the win probability actually bled away in the pre-endgame stage (84.8% lost across 15 errors, the largest share of the total), with ordinary tactical misplays outweighing missed bingos overall — though the single costliest error was itself a missed bingo: against Laurie Cohen, holding ACENOTT, Jesse played D8 CO(L)TAN for 28 instead of 10H ATTONCE for 70, a 19.0% win probability swing. Bingo-finding was strong at 81.5% (22/27) against opponents' 52.9%, though five bingos slipped by (ATTONCE, O(U)TSIZES, BIAT(H)LE(T)E, sHEB(E)(E)NER, ROSELLA). Note that under this VOID challenge rule no phonies are possible for either side, so the clean play here isn't a discipline achievement, and one reported figure — average mistakes score — actually disagrees with the official woogles.io league table, so treat that number with caution.
19a0eadf-f17a-409e-bf32-46543a2fd6fd.title: Collins League - Season 18

331d202e-0e1b-4af2-9559-ec30cb9bc928.summary_md: Jesse swept the NSC 2019 Final 2-0 against Austin Shin, outscoring him +175 across the two games (507-430 and 513-415). The play was sharp and bingo-heavy — a perfect 7-for-7 bingo find rate, 4 bingos in the Round 1 win alone, and a tidy 1.2 average mistakes score against Austin's 2.05. With no phonies on either side of the ledger, this was a clean, commanding finish to the tournament.
331d202e-0e1b-4af2-9559-ec30cb9bc928.title: NSC 2019 Final

342e1637-8b17-458c-b367-b9b3ba753cbb.summary_md: A tough round-robin battle against Nigel Richards that ended 3-4 with a −169 aggregate spread. Jesse's bingo-finding was sharp — 19/20 (95%) — highlighted by a four-bingo, 60-point-endgame Round 3 win (459-363) that included a DERMES* phony, and a gutsy Round 4 victory (433-402) despite missing PaRROTI(E)(R
342e1637-8b17-458c-b367-b9b3ba753cbb.title: 2019 WESPAC Final

38341b8a-a16b-4cd6-96f5-5b4c01864f95.summary_md: Jesse finished WESPAC 2023 at 16-11 with a healthy +846 spread, anchored by a strong 89.7% bingo find rate (61/68) and a solid 2.22 average mistakes score across 27 games. The high point was a 586-360 demolition of Wayne Kelly, part of a stretch of blowout wins over Terry Kang (+209), Dr Wenwa Akinyi (+194), and Joanne Craig (+157), while the toughest defeats came against Weibin (−180, facing five opposing bingos) and Neil Scott (−142, undone by a 56-point endgame swing and a costly ABJOIN phony). Close games went both ways, from a nervy +2 win over Odette Rio to one-point-per-tile losses like the −15 heartbreaker against Paul Allan and −18 against Lewis Mackay. Overall, disciplined play defined the run — only two missed bingos of note (UNMASKER in Round 2, GAROTTED/HIPIDATE in Round 20 among them) — even as a few high-mistake rounds against Bob Jackman and Jared Robinson show where a bit more precision could have padded the record further.
38341b8a-a16b-4cd6-96f5-5b4c01864f95.title: WESPAC 2023 (Las Vegas)

47dba05b-b56a-4a26-affb-55e023fb77f8.summary_md: Jesse closed out Hood River 2022 with a strong 15-5 record and a commanding +1638 spread, headlined by three separate 600-point monster games against Lola (608), Jennifer Clinchy (583), and Betty Cornelison (604). Play was sharp overall — a 91.5% bingo find rate (54/59) and just 2 phonies over 20 games — with only five bingos missed all tournament: ANT(I)LEFT and GUESTEN in the Round 5 loss to Mike McKenna, ThALLUS in the Round 9 loss to Conrad, and EYEBOLT/GLYCOSE in the Round 15 win over Josh Castellano. The five losses were largely close, competitive games (Ruth Hamilton by just 1, Bing by 102 in the roughest outing at MI=3.8), showing the losses came from tight equity margins rather than any single blowout. Opponents combined for only 6 phonies and a perfect 100% bingo find rate on limited annotated data, underscoring that Jesse's dominant spread was built on his own high-powered offense rather than opponent weakness.
47dba05b-b56a-4a26-affb-55e023fb77f8.title: Hood River 2022

55b29df3-10fd-471b-9e87-135ed5bbb2f6.summary_md: Jesse Day put together a dominant 58-19 run against James Curley, racking up a +5238 spread across 77 games and posting a strong 90.2% bingo find rate (202/224) with a lean 2.18 average mistakes score. The margins were often lopsided — monster wins of +655, +621, +599, +583, and +575 — while the losses tended to come in tighter, error-prone games (like the −200 Round 21 defeat, where three bingos were missed in a single sitting). Curley stayed competitive throughout with his own 74.5% bingo find rate across annotated games, but couldn't match Jesse's consistency over the long haul, missing bingos like GRANARY, HYALINE, and BRISANT along the way.
55b29df3-10fd-471b-9e87-135ed5bbb2f6.title: James Curley practice games

56fd9e2f-07d9-4a43-beb9-30e1d432843e.summary_md: A best-of-three final against Nigel Richards ended 1-2 with a punishing −304 aggregate spread. Jesse's play was largely sound — 1.73 average mistakes score, a 75% bingo find rate, and zero phonies — but Round 1 got away from him early, a 374-685 blowout that left too much ground to make up. Round 2 was the highlight, a 563-417 win built on four bingos, yet Nigel answered with four bingos of his own in Round 1 and a near-perfect 0.40 mistakes score across the annotated games, and a tight 296-435 Round 3 loss sealed the match in his favor.
56fd9e2f-07d9-4a43-beb9-30e1d432843e.title: King's Cup 2019 Finals

7c16ae2b-ec5a-4606-8612-3f2d92f77c64.summary_md: Jesse Day finished WESPAC 2019 at 20-10 (+1331), anchored by a stellar bingo find rate (77/80, 96.2%) and a low average mistakes score of 1.68, well ahead of opponents' 1.87. Dominant wins came against Victor Tung (+241), Yong Jian Rong (+189), Olatunde Oduwale (+182), and Dr Bing (+192), with near-flawless games against Rahil Parkar, Enoch Nwali, and Nigel Richards (all under 1.0 MI). The rough patch was a five-round stretch against Allan Oyende, Tarin, Olatunde, and Hubert Wee, where three straight losses and a pair of nail-biters (−1 vs Olatunde, −1 vs Allan Oyende at 4.7 MI) cost momentum. Only three bingos were missed all event (Rd24's B(E)RRiGAN and ONAGERs, Rd32's (G)OREFEST), underscoring how disciplined the bulk of the play was despite the mid-tournament slump.
7c16ae2b-ec5a-4606-8612-3f2d92f77c64.title: WESPAC 2019

96e9f89d-348b-47ac-ae43-aeb019c4a96a.summary_md: Jesse ran the table in Collins League Season 19, going a perfect 14-0 with a staggering +2422 aggregate spread, highlighted by 599 and 637-point blowouts against Ishika S and Zain Marfani respectively. The bingo output was outstanding — 35 of 36 bingos found (97.2%) against a field that converted only 44.1% of theirs — with dominant wins like +272 over Sukanya Baba and +357 over Zain Marfani. Most win probability actually leaked away in the middle game (26 errors, 66.3% of win probability lost), driven almost entirely by ordinary tactical missteps rather than missed bingos; the single costliest error came in Round 5 against Devon Dublin, exchanging AEIIIMU for zero points instead of playing 3C UMIA(Q) for 34, a 9.2% swing. With a 1.83 mistakes score placing 4th of 207 qualified players league-wide, this was a commanding, near-flawless title run.
96e9f89d-348b-47ac-ae43-aeb019c4a96a.title: Collins League - Season 19

b2aa32e7-ab1d-45c2-8d59-362eeec37cb1.summary_md: Jesse Day finished NSC 2019 at a solid 20-9 (+1689), highlighted by a dominant 614-368 win over Dean Saldanha in Round 8 and a 580-296 blowout of Jason Keller in Round 26, offset by tight one-possession losses to Tony Leah (434-436) and Nick Ball (494-506). Bingo-finding was excellent all week (76/78, 97.4%), with only two misses — GRANOLa in Round 5 and RINGL(E)TY in Round 27 — both of which turned winnable games into losses or narrow escapes. Five phonies were played across the event (DAUK, PONDIEST, HOMEYEST, TIRINGLY, and TILTY/TE), while opponents Josh Castellano, Jason Keller, Tony Leah, and David Whitley combined to miss seven bingos of their own, including Keller's SIRLOIN in the Round 26 rout. The overall mistake profile (avg 12.5 vs. opponents' 32.0) reflects a consistently sharper game than the field, even through a rocky mid-tournament stretch of four losses in five rounds (Rds 9-11, 14).
b2aa32e7-ab1d-45c2-8d59-362eeec37cb1.title: NSC 2019

cf677d39-81ad-4a59-aec9-227c38340572.summary_md: Jesse finished 9-10 (+144) at Causeway 2026, a middling record built on streaky play — a 605-449 monster over Austin Shin and a +161 blowout of Vannitha Balasingam bookending tougher losses like the 363-556 blowout to Josh Castellano and back-to-back defeats to Soramet (−113, −112). The bingo game was strong (41/50, 82%), but nine bingos went unfound over the event, including cOEXtEN(D) in Round 3, U(T)ILIZERS in Round 9, and IN(T)ERIO(R)S in a heartbreaking 476-479 loss to Chollapat in Round 18. Round 17 against Euclid Hui was the cleanest performance of the tournament at just 0.4 mistakes, while Round 19's 419-421 nail-biter to Odette Rio showed the equity leaks (4.1 mistakes) that cropped up on the rougher days. Opponents phonied five times to Jesse's one, but with no challenge rule specified those numbers reflect volume of play more than discipline.
cf677d39-81ad-4a59-aec9-227c38340572.title: Jesse Day's (abbreviated) Causeway 2026

d1212bee-bc38-4f19-8619-6be460686182.summary_md: Jesse went 5-1 (+500) at the Austin One-Day, with wins over Michael Donegan (482-296), Anuj Shetty (547-362), James Curley (395-359), and Becky Dyer twice (524-452, 497-423), with the lone loss to Chris Canik (384-437) after Canik found three bingos. Play was efficient overall — a 1.98 average mistakes score and a strong 85.7% bingo find rate (12/14) — with Rounds 1 and 6 standing out as especially clean (0.6 and 0.8 MI). The Round 3 game against Curley was the shakiest of the day, a narrow 36-point win marred by two missed bingos, COURAN(T)O and DOGGEDl(Y).
d1212bee-bc38-4f19-8619-6be460686182.title: Austin One-Day Aug '23

ffe31e07-d5fb-4937-bc08-691958053a8e.summary_md: Jesse opened the final with a commanding 541-391 win over Nigel Richards, but dropped the next three to fall 1-3 for a −214 aggregate. The damage came in bursts — a 307-536 blowout in Round 2 and a 452-575 loss in Round 4 — while Round 3 was a heartbreaker, lost by just 12 points despite Nigel passing up WIS(E)LIER. Jesse found bingos at a 63.6% clip and stayed phony-free, but four missed bingos (DOGSTAI(L) and b(E)HOVELy in Round 1, (T)RUNNELS and (O)(S)CITATED in Round 4) left points on the board against an opponent who found bingos at a brutal 90.9% rate.
ffe31e07-d5fb-4937-bc08-691958053a8e.title: 2018 World Scrabble Championship Finals
